decision_summary: The E3 candidate achieved high in-distribution performance on Tiny-GenImage (BalAcc 0.8520, AUC 0.9453), but rigorous generalization audits revealed critical defects that prohibit production deployment: 1. Severe cross-dataset degradation on the modern Frontier benchmark (BalAcc 0.5497 vs Baseline 0.6228; AUC 0.5546 vs Baseline 0.6501). 2. Catastrophic shortcut learning on image format: matched transcoding showed that converting AI PNG images to JPEG caused 45.6% to 49.5% prediction flips, with a mean logit shift of 6.12 to 6.71 points. 3. Sharp recall drop on held-out unseen generators: Midjourney (51.6%), Wukong (54.0%), and VQDM (20.6%). Consequently, the baseline model is retained in production, and E3 is rejected for deployment.

evaluation_criteria_audit.cross_dataset_performance: FAIL (E3 underperformed Baseline on Frontier by -7.31% BalAcc and -9.55% AUC)
evaluation_criteria_audit.unseen_generator_generalization: PASS_WITH_LIMITATIONS (Improved BalAcc over baseline due to specificity, but recall collapsed to 20-54%)
evaluation_criteria_audit.encoding_robustness: FAIL (45.6% - 49.5% flip rate under JPEG transcoding; severe format confounding)
evaluation_criteria_audit.compression_robustness: FAIL (E3 dropped to ~0.54-0.56 AUC across social media variants, below baseline ~0.64-0.66)
evaluation_criteria_audit.confidence_calibration: PASS (Optimal T=2.0898 on Tiny-GenImage; pooled T=2.2729; significantly improved over baseline)

phase7_recommendations: 1. Retain the frozen CIFAKE baseline (models/baselines/siglip_frozen_head.pt) in production.

2. For future fine-tuning (Phase 7), apply aggressive data augmentation including random JPEG compression, format transcoding, and blur during training to break the 100% JPEG (real) vs 100% PNG (AI) artifact shortcut.
3. Incorporate multi-generator, format-balanced training data across both real and synthetic partitions.
